title: A codec setting that changes payloads but not what the module can do
summary: Message properties are now written in alphabetical order, so that payloads in logs and dead-letter topics diff cleanly. The wire format changes, but the module reaches exactly the same JDK capabilities and libraries as before, and the capability contract passes untouched.

change.description: Enable Jackson's alphabetical property ordering on the shared mapper. Operations asked for it: when two copies of a message are compared in a log viewer, the fields should line up.

risk: None for the capability contract. The example is here to show its selectivity: it is not a diff of the code or of the output, but of what the compiled module is able to do. A change to serialization order, however visible on the wire, is invisible to it, so the gate stays quiet for the everyday changes that make up most of a module's history.
explanation: The verifier recomputes the module's capability contract from the new bytecode and compares it with the checked-in one. The new code calls one more Jackson method on the builder, which is a call into a library the contract already lists, and no JDK entry point of any capability. The two contracts are identical, so the build passes without a contract change, and the pull request contains only the code.
provenance: Constructed as the counterpart of example 009.
